title: Predicting drug-induced liver injury
line: liver toxicity in chemical space, starting from the FDA's own reference set
question: Drug-induced liver injury is a leading reason drugs are withdrawn or restricted. How well does chemical structure alone separate the drugs that injure the liver from those that don't, and where does it fail?
data: FDA DILIrank (Chen et al., Drug Discovery Today 2016): about a thousand drugs ranked by liver-injury concern
planned: prior art first: DILIrank and the published DILI prediction models set the bar, so this starts by reproducing a baseline rather than claiming a new one.
a chemical-space map of the DILIrank drugs, coloured by concern level, with the misclassified ones labelled on hover.
a successor to my 2022 Chemception hepatotoxicity model (in Earlier work), which trained a CNN on molecule images.
